chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghayath ibn Ibrahim from Ja'far from his father, peace be upon them both:

That Ali (peace be upon him), when he took a false witness, if he was a stranger, he sent him to his tribe, and if he was a townsman, he sent him to his market, and he had him paraded around, then he detained him for a few days, then he released him.

key_terms.غَرِيباً: Stranger (one residing outside their native tribe/area)

ai.seo_question: What was the punishment for a false witness according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration highlights Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) pragmatic judicial approach, where the penalty for a false witness (*shahid al-zur*) was tailored to the individual's social context—parading them in their native tribe or local market to maximize public exposure. This method served not only as a deterrent but also as a restorative measure, ensuring the community directly witnessed the correction of the lie before the witness was released. It reflects the Shia emphasis on contextual justice (*adl*) and the practical application of *ta'zir* (discretionary punishment) by the Imam.
